name: Carmilla
description: The languid vampire of Styria who loved her victims before she drained them
legend: Le Fanu, a Dublin journalist and novelist, serialised Carmilla in the magazine The Dark Blue from December 1871 to March 1872 and collected it that year in In a Glass Darkly, framed as a case from the papers of the occult doctor Martin Hesselius. Laura, a lonely girl in a castle in Styria, takes in the survivor of a carriage accident, who turns out to be the long-dead Countess Mircalla Karnstein with her name reshuffled. It came out 25 years before Dracula, and Bram Stoker read it closely: his early notes placed Dracula's castle in Styria, and the deleted opening later published as 'Dracula's Guest' features a vampire countess from Gratz. Le Fanu's vampire is a woman who preys on women, and that has kept the story in print, on screen and in argument ever since.

myths.claim: Carmilla came after Dracula and copied it.
myths.explanation: Carmilla was published in 1872, 25 years before Dracula (1897). Stoker was the borrower.

myths.claim: Carmilla can take the form of a cat.
myths.explanation: Laura sees a huge, sooty-black cat creeping about her bedroom before the attacks, and the General's niece was visited by the same beast.

myths.claim: Le Fanu's vampire is destroyed by sunlight.
myths.explanation: Carmilla is up and about in the afternoons, just late and listless. She is finished the old-fashioned way: a stake, beheading and burning, with the ashes thrown into the river.

myths.claim: The vampire's names are anagrams of each other.
myths.explanation: Mircalla, Millarca and Carmilla rearrange the same letters, which is the clue that unmasks her.

myths.claim: Carmilla lies in a coffin full of blood.
myths.explanation: When her tomb is opened, the body is found immersed in seven inches of blood, with a faint heartbeat and open eyes.

quotes.text: You are mine, you shall be mine, you and I are one for ever.
quotes.speaker: Carmilla

quotes.text: I live in your warm life, and you shall die—die, sweetly die—into mine.
quotes.speaker: Carmilla

powers: Taking the shape of a great black cat
A deathless beauty that disarms suspicion
Turning her victims' affection into surrender
weaknesses: Hymns and funerals, which make her ill
A lie-in that stretches past noon
A stake, an axe and a fire
legacy: Vampyr (1932), Carl Theodor Dreyer's dreamlike film loosely drawn from In a Glass Darkly
Blood and Roses (1960), Roger Vadim's modern-dress version
Hammer's The Vampire Lovers (1970), with Ingrid Pitt as Carmilla
Lust for a Vampire (1971) and Twins of Evil (1971), the rest of Hammer's Karnstein trilogy
Carmilla (2014), the web series that gave the story a new fandom
facts: Carmilla was published 25 years before Dracula
The story is narrated by Laura, the vampire's victim and friend
It is set in Styria, in Austria, where Stoker's early plans put Dracula's castle too
Carmilla, Mircalla and Millarca are all anagrams of the same name
She can take the form of a huge black cat
Her tomb is opened and the body found lying in blood, with a faint heartbeat
The story was serialised in the magazine The Dark Blue and collected in In a Glass Darkly in 1872
hostIntro: Tonight's guest arrived by carriage, rather suddenly, and would love to stay a while. She's a little tired in the mornings, so do keep your voice down, and your collar up.
